audit.why: Difficulty 6/10 FAV matches the 52.5% win rate over 2657 games; lane is an execution test decided at Level 3 and around World Ender.
audit.corrected: Left as-is; Level 1 why rewritten to name the real opener tell.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[5].side and win[5] gave the first-item window to Riven while whys[5] and spikes[2] both call it Aatrox's ownership window, and the packet levelChart has Aatrox there.
audit.why: Aatrox's first-item sustain plus Deathbringer Stance and World Ender healing outlast Riven's burst; the page contradicted itself and the packet.
audit.corrected: First-item row flipped to Aatrox in both layers, with phases[5].why restated to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Deathbringer Stance (P) auto-reset opener was never mentioned, and wants.foe[2] called Infernal Chains a 'chain-snare'.
audit.why: Riot's text for Infernal Chains is a drag-back plus slow, not a snare; the mirror audit flagged the derived grounding flag as unsupported too. Aatrox's burst starts on a passive-empowered auto reset, so the wind-up is the cue, not the ability cast.
audit.corrected: whys[0] now names the Deathbringer Stance reset as the step-back tell; wants.foe[2] names Infernal Chains (W) with its 20s rank-1 cooldown as a drag, not a snare. No grounding claim made.

audit.whatIsWrong: mid stated World Ender is 'a 100-second cooldown at rank 1'.
audit.why: Riot data has World Ender at 120/100/80 — 120s at rank 1, 100s at rank 2.

edits.before: Both kits are threatening at Level 1 but neither has a clean combo — your Q resets chip and his Q poke chips back; respect range and set up the wave.
edits.after: Both are threatening at Level 1 with no clean combo — his opener is a Deathbringer Stance auto reset, so step back on the wind-up, not on the Q cast.

edits.before: Pull you into his W chain-snare after your E is committed so you can't dodge the third Q knockup
edits.after: Land Infernal Chains (W, 20s) and drag you back once your E is spent so the Q3 knockup cannot be dodged

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are an execution test: Aatrox's passive heals mean dragged-out trades let him claw back damage you already dealt, so your job is to end the combo fast and walk out before his drain kicks in. At Level 6 you get Wind Slash as an execute threat — bait his World Ender by faking a recall or shove, let him burn it, then all-in immediately on the World Ender cooldown so he can't drain-tank your burst. His R is a 100-second cooldown at rank 1; track it like you track his Q.
